guide.summary: Forgejo documents an instance-wide OAuth2 provider with an authorization code flow, but OAuth scopes are not implemented and third-party tokens have administrative rights, so the read-only boundary cannot be enforced by the token. Repository listing is documented through the search endpoint with page and limit pagination. Setup happens on each customer's own instance.

findings.title: OAuth2 provider is documented for third-party apps

findings.appliesWhen: Applies to each customer's own Forgejo instance acting as provider.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 provider Forgejo supports acting as an OAuth2 provider to allow third party applications to access its resources with the user’s consent.

findings.title: OAuth apps are registered on the instance admin page
findings.detail: On an instance acting as provider, OAuth2 applications are created at /admin/applications. The client secret is shown only once after registration.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the customer's instance uses Forgejo as the instance-wide provider; the customer administrator owns this step.

findings.title: Authorization code flow requires matching redirect URI
findings.detail: Send the user to the authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and state, then exchange the returned code at the access token endpoint. The redirect URI must match in both requests.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the individual customer's consent and token exchange on their instance.

The REDIRECT_URI in the access_token request must match the REDIRECT_URI in the authorize request.

findings.title: OAuth scopes are not implemented, so no narrower read grant can be requested
findings.detail: Forgejo documents that OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented. Scoped access tokens are a separate mechanism and are entirely different from OAuth2.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to any OAuth token issued by the instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scoped tokens or personal access tokens are entirely different from OAuth2;

findings.title: Third-party OAuth tokens carry administrative rights
findings.detail: Third-party applications that obtain a token for a user through an OAuth2 application have administrative rights. The read-only intent is therefore not enforced by the token.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every OAuth token issued by the instance, including the token used for the listing test.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Repository listing uses the search endpoint
findings.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search includes private repositories the user can access by default. The user repositories endpoint lists only repositories the user owns, so it is not used for visible repositories.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
## GET /api/v1/user/repos | List the repos that the authenticated user owns

findings.title: Pagination uses page and limit with Link headers
findings.detail: The API takes page and limit parameters. Link headers include next and last links and x-total-count gives the total. The default and maximum page size come from the settings API.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to repeated listing until no next link is returned.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"

findings.title: OAuth access token uses the Bearer authorization header
findings.detail: Send the OAuth access token in an Authorization Bearer header. API tokens use a separate header format.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to each resource request made with an OAuth token.

evidence.quote: HTTP basic authentication Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

steps.title: List the first page of visible repository names
steps.detail: Run one GET to /api/v1/repos/search with the OAuth access token sent as Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN. Use the test account only, because OAuth tokens from third-party applications carry administrative rights. Private repositories the user can access are included by default. Representative input: limit=50 and page=1. Expected result: a JSON list of repositories visible to the connected test account. Boundary check: confirm the request log shows only GET requests and no create, edit or delete calls; compare the returned names with the test account's visible repositories.
steps.doneWhen: Page 1 is retrieved, the names are compared with the test account's view, and only GET requests were sent.

Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access token for the test account

steps.title: Continue listing until no next link is returned
steps.detail: Repeat the same GET with page incremented by one (page=2, page=3, and so on) and limit=50 while the Link response header contains rel=next; you may instead follow the returned next link unchanged. Stop only when no rel=next link is returned. x-total-count gives the total number of items to check the collected count against. Representative input: page=2. Expected result: each page adds repositories until the documented end. Boundary check: confirm all requests are GET and no write call is made, and that the collected count equals x-total-count.
steps.doneWhen: All pages are retrieved until no rel=next link remains, and the collected count matches x-total-count.

details.detail: Third-party applications that obtain a token for a user through an OAuth2 application have administrative rights. The read-only intent is therefore not enforced by the token.
details.appliesWhen: Applies to every OAuth token issued by the instance, including the token used for the listing test.

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

details.title: Repository listing uses the search endpoint
details.detail: GET /api/v1/repos/search includes private repositories the user can access by default. The user repositories endpoint lists only repositories the user owns, so it is not used for visible repositories.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
## GET /api/v1/user/repos | List the repos that the authenticated user owns

details.title: Pagination uses page and limit with Link headers
details.detail: The API takes page and limit parameters. Link headers include next and last links and x-total-count gives the total. The default and maximum page size come from the settings API.
details.appliesWhen: Applies to repeated listing until no next link is returned.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"

details.title: OAuth access token uses the Bearer authorization header
details.detail: Send the OAuth access token in an Authorization Bearer header. API tokens use a separate header format.
details.appliesWhen: Applies to each resource request made with an OAuth token.

evidence.quote: HTTP basic authentication Authorization: Bearer ... header in HTTP headers
Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.
